props.title: Signet Jam
props.description: A weekly jam night at one Denver taproom on a Sunday or Monday, run by a professional house band with a sign-up sheet. Twelve weeks to start, then we both decide.

notes._note: Signet Jam, the jam-night pitch page. A PRIVATE SHARE: Daniel sends the link after a first conversation with a venue owner, so it is linked from no nav and no footer, and the noindex keeps it out of the sitemap, llms.txt and search. ?motion=off renders the plain stack. NO VENUE is mentioned anywhere on the page, not even the fallback line, on Daniel's call 2026-09-18 ('no venue should be mentioned'); the ?venue= parameter is gone with it, and no placeholder venue name goes into any URL, screenshot or tab he can see. REBUILT 2026-09-18 on Daniel's call ('if someone comes to this page they're not going to know what's going on'): the page now explains itself from zero, in this order: what a jam night is (hero lede), what it does for a taproom, the deal (venue cost, Signet's side, the twelve-week term), how the night runs, who's running it, the site's client strip, seven owner questions, the close. The ledger lines, the twelve-week line, the host paragraph and 'One venue. Sunday or Monday.' are the 2026-09-16 handoff's; the rest is 2026-09-18 copy written to the copy laws (AI-TELLS, no o'clocks, no projections, no scene-writing, no prices, 'musicians' never 'players'). The fee is Daniel's, 2026-09-18: 'there is a fee. but we are investing early fee into marketing promotions', so the page says there is a fee and the early fee is invested in marketing and promotion for the night, with no figure ever. One reading of the handoff still stands until he strikes it: the band's own PA as Signet's sound. Never put a venue name in a link handed to him. Page-scoped CSS lives in sections/00-style.html, the script in sections/08-script.html. The original handoff is HANDOFF.md in this dir; nothing in it is ratified voice, see the 2026-09-16 note.

props.html:
Signet Jam

A weekly jam night

A live music night at your taproom, every week on a Sunday or Monday, with a professional house band and a sign-up sheet. Musicians from around Denver put their names on the sheet and sit in with the band for a few tunes each. Signet runs the night, and your staff runs the bar the way it always does.

Book a 30-minute call hello@signetartists.com

props.html:
The business case

What a jam does for a taproom

The musicians are the first crowd.

The musicians who come to play are the first hundred people who show up. They're at your bar while they wait to be called up.

Same night, every week.

It's the same night and the same band every week, so anyone who comes once knows when to come back.

A featured act once a month.

Once a month an act with its own following plays the second set, and they bring their own crowd with them.

A clip a week for your accounts.

Every week we cut a clip from the night and send it to you ready to post, with your venue tagged.

On the night

How the night runs

  1. 01

    The house band opens with a set.

    The band plays a full set before anyone from the sheet comes up.

  2. 02

    Musicians sign the sheet at the bar.

    The host calls them up in order, a few tunes each, on songs they already know.

  3. 03

    Once a month, a featured act plays the second set.

  4. 04

    The band closes the night.

    Then the band packs the gear back into your closet until next week.

  5. 05

    We cut it and send it to you ready to post, with your venue tagged.

Who's running it

Signet Jam is run by a seasoned, connected professional musician. The host plays bass for a living, upright and electric, in bands around Denver, and before that built a company to 180 people and sold it. The house band is made up of working musicians who play around Denver every week.

Signet Artists delivers live entertainment for private events in Denver, Colorado and surrounding areas.

props.html:
Questions

Questions owners ask

Is there a fee?
Yes. In the early weeks the fee goes into marketing and promotion for the night, and we'll go over the figure on the call. Beyond the fee, the venue covers a corner of the floor, your normal staff for the night, a closet for the gear, one post a week and a round for the band. At week twelve we both decide whether it continues, and on what terms.
Do we need a stage?
No. The band brings the backline and sets up in a corner of the floor. The gear stays in your closet between nights, so there's no weekly load-in through your front door.
How loud is it?
It's a band with a drummer, so it's as loud as a band in a bar. The host keeps the volume in check from the floor. If your space has a limit, or close neighbors, tell us on the call and we'll plan around it.
Who gets to sit in?
Any musician who signs the sheet. The host sets the order and puts each one on tunes they already know.
What if only a few people sign up the first week?
The house band plays a full night whether the sheet has three names on it or twenty. That's also why the trial is twelve weeks. Neither of us has to judge it on the first night.
Why Sunday or Monday?
They're usually the slowest nights in a taproom, and they're the nights working musicians have off, since the paid gigs are Fridays and Saturdays. If a different night is your slow one, tell us.
What do we have to post?
One post a week from your accounts. We send you the clip already cut and tagged, so all you do is post it.

<script>
(function () {
  'use strict';
  var doc = document, root = doc.documentElement;

  var params = null;
  try { params = new URLSearchParams(location.search); } catch (e) {}

  /* Fade up on enter, once. A scroll check rather than an
     IntersectionObserver: a fast scroll can jump an element clean past the
     viewport between observer frames, and it would then never fire and stay
     invisible. Anything whose top has passed the 88% line is in, including
     anything already scrolled past. ?motion=off or reduced motion: nothing
     moves, everything simply renders. */
  var motionOff = (params && params.get('motion') === 'off')
    || window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
  if (motionOff) { return; }
  root.classList.add('jam-motion');
  var pending = Array.prototype.slice.call(doc.querySelectorAll('.jam-reveal'));
  var ticking = false;
  function check() {
    ticking = false;
    var line = window.innerHeight * 0.88;
    pending = pending.filter(function (el) {
      if (el.getBoundingClientRect().top < line) { el.classList.add('is-in'); return false; }
      return true;
    });
    if (!pending.length) {
      window.removeEventListener('scroll', onScroll);
      window.removeEventListener('resize', onScroll);
    }
  }
  function onScroll() {
    if (!ticking) { ticking = true; window.requestAnimationFrame(check); }
  }
  window.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, { passive: true });
  window.addEventListener('resize', onScroll);
  window.addEventListener('pageshow', onScroll);
  check();
})();
</script>
